title: Algebra-valued complete flags and their scheme-theoretic stabilizers
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $n\geq0$. For a commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and algebra homomorphisms as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], write $A^n$ in coordinates indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. A complete flag over $A$ is a sequence of submodules [def-weil-submodule-span] $0=L_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq L_n=A^n$, each a locally direct summand of constant rank $i$. Equivalently on this affine scheme, each $L_i$ has a complementary submodule, is finite, and has rank $i$ at every prime of $A$. Rank at a prime means the rank of its localization. The type of these flags is $\operatorname{Fl}_n(A)$. A homomorphism $f:A\to B$ extends a submodule by the $B$-span of its coordinatewise image. An invertible matrix preserves a flag when the image of each submodule under its matrix linear map equals that submodule. Given a group-scheme representation $r:G\to\mathrm{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sc-general-linear-group] and a closed subgroup inclusion $i:K\to G$ [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], $i$ is its scheme-theoretic stabilizer at $L\in\operatorname{Fl}_n(k)$ when, for every $k$-algebra $A$ and $g\in G(A)$, $g$ lies in the image of $K(A)$ if and only if $r_A(g)$ preserves the scalar extension of $L$. This includes $n=0$, nonreduced algebras, and the zero algebra.
